features.name: Inboxes, conversations, messages, assignment, labels, teams
Replies to email, WhatsApp, SMS and social channels

workloadAssumptions: One TapeDB workspace per Chatwoot account; a busy account's inbox writes go through one writer.
Live views are per agent; an account with many agents online is the hot case for fan-out.

architecture.summary: A compatible rewrite: TapeDB workspaces per account hold the domain model with access rules; live queries replace ActionCable for inbox and widget; TapeDB presence and broadcast replace the Redis presence set and typing signals; R2 files hold attachments; TapeDB webhooks trigger outgoing events; Queues and Workflows carry provider delivery, retries, SLA timers and auto-resolution, with a delivery ledger in the workspace. No second WebSocket server and no per-conversation Durable Object.

capabilities.description: Typed domain model with serializable writes per account
capabilities.candidate: TapeDB models and transactions in one workspace per account
gaps: The fixture models contacts, conversations, messages, assignment and unread; teams, labels, macros, automation rules, campaigns and the help centre are not modelled.

capabilities.candidate: A workspace per account; claims are scoped to one workspace

capabilities.description: Messages ordered within a conversation, including under concurrent sends
capabilities.candidate: TapeDB's single writer and log sequence
gaps: Ordering of provider-delivered inbound messages depends on provider timestamps and is not covered.

capabilities.description: Live inbox, conversation and widget views
capabilities.candidate: TapeDB live queries over one socket per workspace

capabilities.description: Agent and contact presence and typing indicators
capabilities.candidate: TapeDB presence for availability; broadcast topics for typing
gaps: Presence fan-out grows with the square of the room (60 ms p50 at 200 peers); large accounts should scope presence rooms per inbox or team.
Upstream keeps contacts present for 90 s across widget pings; TapeDB presence ends with the socket.

capabilities.candidate: TapeDB files on R2 with file rules
gaps: File rules decide per file path; mapping them to conversation membership is application work.

capabilities.description: Signed outgoing webhooks for account events
capabilities.candidate: TapeDB webhooks (transactional capture, signed, ordered per endpoint, at-least-once)
gaps: TapeDB's payload is a row change; Chatwoot's webhook payloads are event-shaped (message_created, conversation_status_changed) and need a mapping.
Delivery inspection and retry shipped in 0.4.1 ($webhooks, $webhookRetry).

capabilities.description: Outbound replies through email, WhatsApp, SMS and social providers
capabilities.candidate: Queues consumers per provider, fed by TapeDB webhooks or direct sends, with a delivery ledger row per message in the workspace
gaps: No exactly-once: providers may receive a message twice; the ledger and provider idempotency keys bound it.
Provider quotas and channel rules are per provider.

capabilities.description: Inbound provider webhooks with signature verification
capabilities.candidate: Worker routes per provider writing to the account workspace

capabilities.description: Auto-resolution, SLA monitors and scheduled items
capabilities.candidate: Workflows (sleep and waitForEvent per conversation) or Cron Triggers scanning workspaces
gaps: A per-conversation Workflow per SLA is a design choice not yet benchmarked against a cron scan.

capabilities.candidate: TapeDB filters ($ilike) for simple search; TapeDB vector and hybrid search (one indexed model) for the knowledge base
gaps: No full-text index across messages in TapeDB; $ilike scans.
Vector search indexes one model per deployment.

capabilities.candidate: TapeDB built-in auth (Better Auth) with membership roles
gaps: SAML SSO (omniauth-saml upstream) is not provided.

capabilities.candidate: TapeDB aggregates and named SQL within an account; Basin for cross-account analytics
gaps: TapeDB is not a warehouse; cross-account reports need a separate store.

risks.description: A large account's writes and presence all go through one workspace.
risks.mitigation: Benchmark with the fixture; scope presence rooms per inbox; split an account only if measurements demand it.

risks.description: At-least-once queues can send a reply twice.
risks.mitigation: Ledger row per outbound message with a provider idempotency key where the provider supports one.

costAssumptions.assumption: Every message write and live re-run is billed as Durable Object requests and rows; not modelled yet.
About 3 operations per outbound message plus 1 read per retry.

decisions.title: Use TapeDB live queries and presence instead of a separate WebSocket service
decisions.context: Chatwoot uses ActionCable on Redis for live updates and presence.

options.name: TapeDB live queries and presence
options.tradeoffs: No extra service; verified primitives; presence fan-out limits large rooms.

options.name: A separate WebSocket Durable Object per conversation
options.tradeoffs: Duplicates TapeDB's socket and invalidation; two sources of truth.

decisions.consequences: One socket per account workspace per client; presence rooms are scoped to keep fan-out small.

decisions.title: Queues and Workflows for background work, not TapeDB webhooks alone
decisions.context: Chatwoot runs 18 Sidekiq queues and cron schedules.

options.name: TapeDB webhooks as the job system
options.tradeoffs: Webhooks are row-change delivery to an endpoint, not a job queue; no scheduling.

options.name: Queues and Workflows fed by TapeDB webhooks
options.tradeoffs: Two systems to operate; each does what it is for.

decisions.choice: Queues and Workflows fed by TapeDB webhooks
decisions.consequences: A delivery ledger in the workspace reconciles what the queue did.
